disclaimer: OEVM is a personal, experimental project for learning about AI tools. Much of its code and text was written with an AI assistant, and it will contain mistakes. Charger data comes from the operators and other sources credited on every record, and remains their work. Everything is provided "as is", with no warranty or guarantee of any kind. Always check prices and availability at the charger.

regulation.summary: The Public Charge Point Regulations 2023 set no limit on how often data users may request the data. Regulation 10(5) requires the data to be available free of charge without terms on its use. DfT's guidance allows terms covering the means of access, which is where operators' rate limits come from.

quotes.text: terms and conditions covering the means of access to the data and API(s) are permissible
quotes.source: DfT, Public Charge Point Regulations 2023 guidance

operators.name: char.gy

evidence.note: Re-checked. The page still lists the open locations and tariffs endpoints.

operators.attribution: Contains data from char.gy published under the Public Charge Point Regulations 2023, used in line with the Open Government Licence v3.0.

rate_limit.ours: At least 6 s between requests to the operator's host, measured from the end of the previous request (at most 600 in any hour), retries included.
rate_limit.comparison: No limit published (checked 2026-10-07). The gap is our own choice.
rate_limit.difference_from_regulations: Neither the operator nor the regulations set a limit.
rate_limit.notes: char.gy's open data page states no rate limit. The gap is this project's own choice: 2 seconds until 8 October 2026, then 6 seconds after the feed refused requests from GitHub's servers part-way through the first daily run (see findings).

findings.summary: EVSE statuses are published as WORKING, and in a live run on 2026-10-07 also as FAULTED. Neither is a value in the OCPI 2.2.1 Status list.
findings.handling: Shown as status unknown rather than guessed. Regulation 10(6)(a) uses "working" to mean an OCPI status of available, charging or reserved.

findings.summary: Tariffs are published in three currencies (EUR, USD and GBP). Locations refer only to the GBP tariff.
findings.handling: Only GBP prices are shown, in pence per kWh, which is how regulation 10(6)(d)(iv) describes the price in reference data. Other currencies show as price unknown and are never converted.

findings.summary: Tariff price components give no VAT figure. OCPI 2.2.1 says an omitted VAT means no VAT is applicable.
findings.handling: VAT is not guessed. Prices are shown as published, which OCPI defines as excluding VAT, and marked "excluding VAT, VAT not stated".

findings.summary: The feed sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so web browsers cannot read it directly.
findings.handling: The map will use data fetched by the pipeline, not requests from visitors' browsers.

findings.summary: In the first daily run from a GitHub Actions runner, the locations feed answered HTTP 403 to the request for offset 2900, after 58 pages had been fetched about 2.8 seconds apart. The same request answered normally from another network the same evening. The server returns at most 50 locations a page, so a full fetch takes about 120 requests for locations alone.
findings.handling: char.gy was left out of that run. The gap between requests was raised from 2 to 6 seconds the same day, and the next run (37856014933, the same evening) fetched every page and published 5,948 locations.

operators.name: Clenergy EV

evidence.note: Links "locations" and "tariffs" on api.clenergy.online in "a machine-readable OCPI format" and states no licence, terms or rate limit.

operators.attribution: Contains data from Clenergy EV published under the Public Charge Point Regulations 2023, used in line with the Open Government Licence v3.0.

rate_limit.ours: At least 11 s between requests to the operator's host, measured from the end of the previous request (at most 328 in any hour), retries included.
rate_limit.comparison: No limit published (checked 2026-10-09). The gap is our own choice.
rate_limit.difference_from_regulations: Neither the operator nor the regulations set a limit.
rate_limit.notes: Clenergy EV's open data page states no rate limit. Responses carry X-RateLimit-Limit 6 with no window stated (see findings). The 11 second gap is this project's own choice: it would stay within 6 requests a minute, plus a 1 second margin, if that is what the header means. Each file holds every record, so a full run makes two requests (about 2.2 MB on 2026-10-09).

findings.summary: Responses wrap the records as {"name": "OK", "message": "ok", "data": [...], "error": null, "forcelogout": false}, with no status_code or timestamp. OCPI 2.2.1 section 4.1.7 describes a response object with status_code and timestamp. The records themselves follow OCPI 2.2.1.
findings.handling: The operator file sets response_envelope to data_list, so the adapter accepts a list in data with no status_code and stops if error is set. Every other feed is still checked strictly.

findings.summary: Responses carry X-RateLimit-Limit 6, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers. No page states the window or whether the limit is per path.
findings.handling: Treated as unknown. The project leaves 11 seconds between requests and makes two requests a run.

findings.summary: The feed address contains the word "development".
findings.handling: Used as published, since the operator's open data page links it. The feed health page will show any change.

findings.summary: The operator field is null on every location (1,400 on 2026-10-09), and tariffs have no country_code or party_id.
findings.handling: Locations show Clenergy EV, the name of the operator publishing the feed. Tariff ids use the party GB CEV from the operator file.

findings.summary: Every location's last_updated is the time of the request, so it does not show when a location last changed. Each EVSE's last_updated varies.
findings.handling: Kept as published.

findings.summary: Every location has country GBR, but some coordinates are outside the UK (for example in the Caribbean, Canada and Ireland), and some appear to have latitude and longitude the other way round.
findings.handling: Locations whose coordinates fall outside the map's UK limits are left off the map and listed in the manifest as not mapped. Those limits also take in the Republic of Ireland, so points there are shown as published. Coordinates are never corrected by this project.

findings.summary: 5 of 129 tariffs are in a currency other than GBP (3 EUR, 1 USD, 1 CAD on 2026-10-09).
findings.handling: Their connectors show "Price unknown". Currencies are never converted.

operators.name: GeniePoint

evidence.note: Read in a browser by the repository owner. Links "Locations data" and "Tariffs data" as .json files and states no licence, terms or rate limit.

operators.attribution: Contains data from GeniePoint published under the Public Charge Point Regulations 2023, used in line with the Open Government Licence v3.0.

relay.reason: The files answered HTTP 403 to the first request from a GitHub Actions runner in the first daily run, while answering normally from another network. The repository owner decided to fetch them through the project's relay on Cloudflare Workers, with the project's User-Agent and the same rate limits.

rate_limit.ours: At least 2 s between requests to the operator's host, measured from the end of the previous request (at most 1800 in any hour), retries included.
rate_limit.comparison: No limit published (checked 2026-10-08). The gap is our own choice.
rate_limit.difference_from_regulations: Neither the operator nor the regulations set a limit.
rate_limit.notes: GeniePoint's open data page states no rate limit. The 2 second gap is this project's own choice. Each file holds every record, so a full run makes two requests (about 1.6 MB on 2026-10-08).

findings.summary: The open data page returns a browser check (HTTP 403) to automated requests. The download links, on opendata.geniepoint.co.uk, answer automated requests normally.
findings.handling: The page was read in a browser by the repository owner and its links recorded here. The files are fetched directly.

findings.summary: Each file holds every record in one response (306 locations and 530 tariffs on 2026-10-08), matching X-Total-Count, but sends X-Limit 0. OCPI 2.2.1 describes X-Limit as the maximum number of objects the server can return.
findings.handling: The adapter reads each file in one request and checks the count against X-Total-Count.

findings.summary: The tariffs file repeats 22 tariffs 8 times each (530 records, 376 distinct ids on 2026-10-08). The copies are identical and no location refers to them.
findings.handling: One copy of each is kept and the repeats are logged.

findings.summary: Tariff descriptions (tariff_alt_text) are internal names, such as Tariff_Fast or Tariff_Rapid followed by an id.
findings.handling: Kept as published. Prices are described from the price components, not this text.

findings.summary: The files send no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so web browsers cannot read them directly.
findings.handling: The map will use data fetched by the pipeline, not requests from visitors' browsers.

findings.summary: The Equans website's general terms of use cover linked subsidiary sites and say that, apart from downloads for personal and internal business use, reproduction needs Equans' permission. The open data page says the data must be publicly available in line with the regulations, and states no terms for the data.
findings.handling: The repository owner decided on 2026-10-08 to read the general website terms as not covering the open data files. The reasoning is recorded in the licence section.

findings.summary: One location, "Cheshire East Council - Crewe Civic" (postcode CW1 2JZ), has longitude 2.444352, which is east of the UK. Its postcode is in Crewe, west of the Greenwich meridian.
findings.handling: Left off the map and listed in the manifest as not mapped. Coordinates are never corrected by this project.

findings.summary: In the first daily run from a GitHub Actions runner, the locations file answered HTTP 403 to the first request. The same file answered normally from another network the same evening.
findings.handling: GeniePoint was left out of that run and the feed health page shows the failure. The repository owner decided the same day to fetch it through the project's relay (see relay above). The owner chose not to contact GeniePoint about the refusal. The first run through the relay (37860826824, the same evening) fetched both files, 306 locations and 530 tariff records, and published 305 locations.

operators.name: Jolt

evidence.note: Read in a browser by the project owner. Gives the Reference Data API URL with a shared apiKey and the Pricing Reference API URL.
Re-read through the help centre's article data. Unchanged; last updated 2025-01-30.

operators.attribution: Contains data from Jolt published under the Public Charge Point Regulations 2023, used in line with the Open Government Licence v3.0.

missing_publish_flag.basis: Jolt publishes this feed itself "In accordance with the UK Public Charge Point Regulations (PCPR) Open Data requirement", and none of its locations has a publish flag. The repository owner decided that locations with no flag may be shown. A flag set to false would still be respected.

rate_limit.ours: At least 2 s between requests to the operator's host, measured from the end of the previous request (at most 1800 in any hour), retries included.
rate_limit.comparison: No limit published (checked 2026-10-08). The gap is our own choice.
rate_limit.difference_from_regulations: Neither the operator nor the regulations set a limit.
rate_limit.notes: Jolt's page states no rate limit (re-read 2026-10-08). The 2 second gap is this project's own choice. A full run makes one request for locations and one per tariff (6 requests on 2026-10-08).

findings.summary: The help page that gives the open data details returns a browser check (HTTP 403) to automated requests.
findings.handling: The page was read in a browser on 2026-10-07. On 2026-10-08 the same article, last updated 2025-01-30, was read through the help centre's article data, which automated tools can reach.

findings.summary: Access uses a shared key printed on the help page, rather than a URL that needs no key.
findings.handling: The key is kept in the GitHub Actions secret JOLT_API_KEY and is never committed.

findings.summary: Responses do not use the OCPI 2.2.1 response format (data, status_code, timestamp). All locations come in one response as {"locations": [...]}, with no paging headers, and each tariff comes as a bare object from tariffs/{tariffId}.
findings.handling: A custom adapter reads this format. It stops with an error if a next page link ever appears, so a partial feed is never taken for the whole one.

findings.summary: Locations have no publish flag, which OCPI 2.2.1 requires (none of 72 on 2026-10-08).
findings.handling: Shown under the repository owner's decision recorded in missing_publish_flag, because Jolt publishes the feed as open data under the regulations. A flag set to false would always be respected.

findings.summary: Locations have no id, which OCPI 2.2.1 requires. Their names, such as BAR004, were unique on 2026-10-08. Some locations have no time_zone (7 of 72).
findings.handling: The name is used as the location id, so ids will change if Jolt renames a site. A missing time zone is recorded as unknown.

findings.summary: EVSE statuses are lower case, such as available and charging, and some EVSEs report preparing, which is not an OCPI 2.2.1 status.
findings.handling: A lower-case value that matches an OCPI 2.2.1 status is read as that status. preparing is shown as unknown.

findings.summary: EVSEs have a null uid and no last_updated. evse_id is a number, such as 143, rather than an eMI3 EVSE ID, and connector ids are numbers rather than strings.
findings.handling: evse_id is used as the EVSE uid and no eMI3 EVSE ID is recorded. Statuses are dated with the time they were fetched.

findings.summary: Connectors give the standard CCS2, which is not an OCPI 2.2.1 connector type.
findings.handling: Read as IEC_62196_T2_COMBO, the OCPI 2.2.1 name for the CCS Combo 2 connector.

findings.summary: Many DC connectors give max_amperage 0 alongside a max_electric_power figure (128 of 160 on 2026-10-08).
findings.handling: Power is taken from max_electric_power.

findings.summary: Some connectors list no tariff (24 of 160 on 2026-10-08), and the tariff "UK discounted tariff" (id 13) has an energy price of null.
findings.handling: These show as price unknown.

findings.summary: The feed includes 7 locations named IONITY, such as IONITY Cambridge, with Jolt's party_id JLT and the tariff "Ionity United Kingdom - Roaming Tariff Group: Base tariff". The feed does not say who operates them.
findings.handling: Shown as published, with Jolt named as the operator because the feed gives no operator. Who operates these sites needs checking.

findings.summary: Tariffs give tariff_alt_text as a list of plain strings, and min_price and max_price as plain numbers, where OCPI 2.2.1 uses DisplayText and Price objects.
findings.handling: Alt text is read as text with no language. A min_price or max_price of 0 is read as no minimum or maximum. Any other plain number does not say whether it includes VAT, so that tariff would show as price unknown.

evidence.note: bp pulse's FAQ uses a request form. Whether a contract is also required is not known.

rate_limit.ours: At least 125 s between requests to the operator's host, measured from the end of the previous request (at most 29 in any hour), retries included.

published.text: 30 per 1 hour for the locations endpoint
published.quote: The `locations` endpoint has a rate limit of 30 requests per 1 hour.

published.text: 30 per 1 hour for the locations endpoint (single location)
published.quote: The `locations/{id}` endpoint has a rate limit of 30 requests per 1 hour.

published.text: 30 per 1 hour for the tariffs endpoint
published.quote: The `tariffs` endpoint has a rate limit of 30 requests per 1 hour.

published.text: 1 per 30 seconds for the statuses endpoint
published.quote: The `statuses` endpoint has a rate limit of 1 request per 30 seconds.

rate_limit.comparison: Within every published limit. The strictest needs 120 s between requests; this project waits 125 s, which includes a safety margin.
rate_limit.difference_from_regulations: The operator sets a limit; the regulations set none. DfT guidance allows such terms on access.
rate_limit.notes: One gap of 125 seconds (the 120 seconds the strictest limit needs, plus a safety margin) is kept between any two requests to open-chargepoints.com, shared by every operator served from it, so this project sends it at most 29 requests in any hour. Requests are sent one at a time; Eco-Movement "strongly recommends limiting simultaneous GET requests to a maximum of 5". It recommends retrieving the entire dataset once a day.

findings.summary: Eco-Movement's PCPR API documentation gives two different defaults for the page size (1000 on the getting started page, 1 in the endpoint reference), and its user guide says date_from works for locations only while the tariffs reference lists it.
findings.handling: This project will always send an explicit page size and test date_from before relying on it.

findings.summary: The rate limits are published, but the documentation does not say whether they apply per key or per address, what kind of time window is used, or what response is sent when a limit is reached.
findings.handling: This project assumes the strictest reading: one allowance shared by every endpoint and every operator on this host, so it waits 125 seconds between any two requests to it.

rate_limit.ours: At least 2 s between requests to the operator's host, measured from the end of the previous request (at most 1800 in any hour), retries included.
rate_limit.comparison: The operator's pages have not been checked for limits yet.

evidence.note: The page offers a form to request an API key. The form asks the requester to confirm they have read and agree to Gridserve's API access and fair use terms.

rate_limit.ours: At least 31 s between requests to the operator's host, measured from the end of the previous request (at most 117 in any hour), retries included.

published.quote: The default API call limit is 1 request per 30 seconds per API key.

rate_limit.comparison: Within every published limit. The strictest needs 30 s between requests; this project waits 31 s, which includes a safety margin.
rate_limit.difference_from_regulations: The operator sets a limit; the regulations set none. DfT guidance allows such terms on access.
rate_limit.notes: Gridserve's API Fair Use Policy sets the limit above, says "Default rate limits are set to 1 call every 30 seconds", and says limits may change. This project waits 31 seconds between any two requests to the host (30 seconds plus a safety margin). The developer documentation (version 1.0, November 2024) states no limit.

findings.summary: The developer documentation's example responses put results under "locations", "location" or "tariffs" keys, while OCPI 2.2.1 responses put them in a "data" field.
findings.handling: The adapter will be written against real responses, recorded as fixtures, not the examples.

findings.summary: The developer documentation lists location-id under "Headers", although the endpoint is written as GET /locations/{location-id}.
findings.handling: Noted for when the adapter is built; the path form will be tested first.

findings.summary: The API Fair Use Policy sets a default limit of 1 request per 30 seconds per API key; the developer documentation (version 1.0, November 2024) states no limit.
findings.handling: This project follows the published limit with a safety margin: 31 seconds between requests.

findings.summary: Keys are requested through a form that asks the requester to agree to the API Fair Use Policy. The policy says intellectual property in the API Data remains Gridserve's and describes the data as confidential and proprietary.
findings.handling: On 2026-10-09 the repository owner decided that regulation 10(5) takes priority over the policy's terms for the data, and that the project goes ahead without first writing to Gridserve. The policy's rate limit is still followed. The operator stays switched off until a key is granted and the adapter is built.

evidence.note: InstaVolt's page refers to an "Open Data Agreement".
